key_insight: Distributed neural controllers can improve pre-stabilized plug-and-play networks while preserving nominal stability through gain-bounded parametrizations valid at every training iterate.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables neural performance upgrades for modular systems such as DC microgrids without stability-constrained optimization or projection steps.
method: Use Internal Model Control to reduce stability assurance to a finite ℓ₂-gain requirement on an auxiliary neural operator.
Interconnect local neural operators through neighbor-only communication and enforce a prescribed network gain bound by construction.
Choose local compositional bounds for selective plug-and-play updates or a network-norm bound for potentially lower conservatism.
evidence_signal: A plug-and-play DC-microgrid case study reports improved voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.
watch_item: Local bounds may be conservative, while the network-norm alternative requires network-wide information; the abstract does not establish robustness to model mismatch.
paper_title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
